sam (applied-ml): Hey — onboarding a HF model and the sampled outputs on Redwood look systematically more repetitive. gen config from HF was copied into generation_config.json and into our mapping. Anyone seen similar? :thinking:

maria (ml-eng): Hmm. Which fields did you map? temp/top_p/top_k/rep_penalty?

sam (applied-ml): Yup. Exact copy: temperature=0.7, top_k=50, top_p=0.95, repetition_penalty=1.1. We also kept do_sample=true. HF eval locally looked fine. On Redwood results have repeated phrases ~20% more.

ryan (infer-runtime): Two quick suspects: special token handling (BOS/EOS) and different interpretation of repetition_penalty in our runtime vs HF's transformers. Also quantization can change effective logits scale, making same temperature behave differently.

maria (ml-eng): I reproduced with a minimal prompt. Found two edge cases:
1) tokenizer.bos_token present in model config + our chat template that prepends <s> => double BOS tokens, so model sees prefix twice and tends to repeat.
2) HF repetition_penalty is applied by multiplying logits for *repeated token ids*; in our runtime we had a legacy implementation that applied an additive penalty on log-probs (sign flipped for one path) — effectively weaker penalty. Fixed in a patch branch and saw repetition drop.

sam (applied-ml): Oof. For 1) how do we detect/normalize when converting config.json -> generation_config.json?

maria (ml-eng): Proposal: during HF->Redwood import, check tokenizer.special_tokens_map and model_config for bos_token_id/eos_token_id/pad_token_id. If chat_template includes an explicit <s> or system prompt with BOS, strip the automatic prepend or set skip_special_tokens=true. Add conversion note.

teresa (docs): Can you paste a small snippet we can include in the onboarding docs?

maria (ml-eng): Sure. Quick example conversion snippet:

```json
// HF generation_config.json
{"do_sample": true, "temperature": 0.7, "top_k": 50, "top_p": 0.95, "repetition_penalty": 1.1}

// Suggested Redwood mapping (values kept as numbers where compatible)
{"temperature": 0.7, "top_k": 50, "top_p": 0.95, "repetition_penalty": 1.1, "do_sample": true}
```

maria (ml-eng): But also add these heuristics in the importer:
- If top_k <= 0 or top_k == null in HF, set top_k = null (our runtime treats 0 as keep top 0 which is invalid).
- If do_sample is false in HF, ignore top_p/top_k (they're not applied).
- If repetition_penalty ~ 1.0 and quantized int8 path, nudge temperature by +0.03-0.08 in a heuristics table.

ryan (infer-runtime): For repetition_penalty differences I logged our old code vs HF. Old (buggy) path:

```python
# buggy: used add instead of multiply
logits[token] = logits[token] - (repetition_penalty - 1.0)
# correct HF semantics (multiplicative)
logits[token] = logits[token] / repetition_penalty
```

ryan (infer-runtime): Patch ready. We'll run a quick A/B on the canary pool.

sam (applied-ml): Nice. Any issues with top_p behavior? I saw outputs with top_p=0.92 still returning low diversity on long prompts.

maria (ml-eng): That's usually due to prefix caching + batching: if we reuse KV cache across variants, and cache is keyed incorrectly (missing role tokens), the effective distribution can get skewed. Also probability mass near tail can be like 1e-8 and numeric underflow in int8 kernels can clamp.

ryan (infer-runtime): We're adding unit tests: generate with synthetic logits and ensure top_k/top_p implementations match HF for the same quantization path. Also test the do_sample=false path explicitly. CI bot will run these. @ci-bot can you add nightly job?

ci-bot: scheduled nightly job "hf-to-redwood-genparam-regressions" added to runner pool.

sam (applied-ml): Great. For docs: can we include a short checklist for model bring-up so PMs don't hit this again?

teresa (docs): I'll draft. Proposed checklist items: tokenizer special tokens audit, generation_config parity check, quantization temp adjustment suggestions, canary A/B with repeated-prompt fuzzing.

maria (ml-eng): Also add a tiny JSON test vector set we can check into model repo: short prompts that exercise repetition and truncation. Example:
```json
{"prompt":"Summarize: The cat sat on the mat.\n\n","expected_non_repetitive":true}
```

sam (applied-ml): One more note — HF has top_k default 50 in some pipelines; our Redwood default is null (unconstrained). Importer should not silently change that; preserve explicit defaults or add a field source: "from_hf" so operators know.

maria (ml-eng): Agreed. I'll update the importer and open a PR with:
- fix repetition_penalty semantics
- special token normalization
- top_k/top_p/do_sample mapping rules
- quantization heuristics (temp nudges) + unit tests

ryan (infer-runtime): I'll run canary once PR lands.

teresa (docs): tagging this for docs and release notes.

sam (applied-ml): Thanks all, that helps. Will re-run evals tomorrow and post numbers. :+1:
